title.zh: 卷111 志八十六 选举六 考绩
title.en: Volume 111 Treatises 86: Selection and Examinations 6, Kao Ji
title.raw: 卷111 志八十六 选举六 考绩

sentences.zh: 志八十六

translations.literal: Treatise eighty-six.
translations.idiomatic: Treatise 86

sentences.zh: 選舉六

translations.literal: Selection and examinations, part six.
translations.idiomatic: Selection and Examinations 6

sentences.zh: 考績

translations.literal: Performance evaluation.
translations.idiomatic: Performance Evaluation

sentences.zh: 三載考績之法，昉自唐、虞。

translations.literal: The method of triennial performance evaluation originated in the eras of Tang and Yu.
translations.idiomatic: The practice of reviewing officials every three years began in the age of Yao and Shun.

sentences.zh: 清沿明制，而品式略殊。

translations.literal: The Qing followed the Ming system, but the grades and forms differed somewhat.
translations.idiomatic: The Qing adopted the Ming framework, though its ranks and procedures differed in detail.

sentences.zh: 京官曰京察，外官曰大計，吏部考功司掌之。

translations.literal: Capital officials were subject to the capital inspection; local officials to the grand assessment; the Department of Merit Records in the Board of Civil Appointments administered both.
translations.idiomatic: Capital officials underwent the capital inspection, local officials the grand assessment, both overseen by the Board of Civil Appointments' Department of Merit Records.

sentences.zh: 京察以子卯午酉歲，部院司員由長官考覈，校以四格，懸「才、守、政、年」為鵠。

translations.literal: The capital inspection was held in the years of zi, mao, wu, and you; clerks of ministries and agencies were examined by their superiors, checked against four criteria, with "talent, integrity, administration, and age" as the standard.
translations.idiomatic: The capital inspection took place in cyclical years marked by zi, mao, wu, and you; department staff were rated by their chiefs against four benchmarks—talent, integrity, administrative performance, and age.

sentences.zh: 分稱職、勤職、供職三等。

translations.literal: They were divided into three grades: fully competent, diligent in duty, and merely adequate.
translations.idiomatic: Ratings fell into three grades: fully competent, diligent, and merely adequate.

sentences.zh: 列一等者，加級記名，則加考引見備外用。

translations.literal: Those placed in the first grade received a step in rank and were recorded by name, then after additional review were presented for possible appointment outside the capital.
translations.idiomatic: First-grade officials received a rank increment and were listed for promotion; after further review they were presented to the throne as candidates for provincial posts.

sentences.zh: 糾以六法，不謹、罷輭者革職，浮躁、才力不及者降調，年老、有疾者休致，註考送部。

translations.literal: Censure followed the six categories: the careless and the weak were dismissed; the frivolous and those lacking capacity were demoted or transferred; the aged and the ill retired; their evaluations were noted and sent to the ministry.
translations.idiomatic: Six categories governed disciplinary action: careless or ineffectual officials were dismissed; frivolous or incapable ones demoted; aged or infirm ones retired—with all evaluations forwarded to the Board.

sentences.zh: 自翰、詹、科、道外，依次過堂。

translations.literal: Apart from the Hanlin Academy, the Court of Imperial Entertainments, the censorate, and the supervising secretaries, the rest passed in review in turn.
translations.idiomatic: Except for Hanlin, Court of Imperial Entertainments, censorate, and supervising-secretary staff, all others were examined in sequence at court.

sentences.zh: 三品京堂由部開列事實，四、五品由王、大臣分別等第，具奏引見取上裁。

translations.literal: Third-rank capital officials had the facts of their service listed by the ministry; fourth- and fifth-rank officials were graded by princes and grand ministers, memorialized, presented, and subject to the throne's decision.
translations.idiomatic: Third-rank metropolitan officials were evaluated on factual records submitted by their ministries; fourth- and fifth-rank officials were graded by princes and senior ministers, memorialized, presented to the throne, and decided by imperial rescript.

sentences.zh: 大計以寅已申亥歲，先期籓、臬、道、府遞察其屬賢否，申之督、撫，督、撫覈其事狀，註考繕冊送部覆覈。

translations.literal: The grand assessment was held in the years of yin, si, shen, and hai; beforehand provincial, judicial, circuit, and prefectural officials successively inspected the merit of their subordinates and reported to governors-general and governors, who verified the facts, noted evaluations, compiled registers, and sent them to the ministry for review.
translations.idiomatic: The grand assessment occurred in years of yin, si, shen, and hai; beforehand provincial, judicial, circuit, and prefectural officers successively reviewed subordinates and reported upward; governors-general and governors verified records, compiled evaluation registers, and submitted them to the Board for final review.

sentences.zh: 才守俱優者，舉以卓異。

translations.literal: Those outstanding in both talent and integrity were recommended as exceptionally excellent.
translations.idiomatic: Officials distinguished in both talent and integrity were nominated as outstanding.

sentences.zh: 劣者，劾以六法。

translations.literal: The inferior were impeached under the six categories.
translations.idiomatic: Deficient officials were impeached under the six disciplinary categories.

sentences.zh: 不入舉劾者為平等。

translations.literal: Those neither recommended nor impeached were classed as average.
translations.idiomatic: Those neither commended nor censured were rated average.

sentences.zh: 卓異官自知縣而上，皆引見候旨。

translations.literal: Outstanding officials from district magistrates upward were all presented to await imperial decree.
translations.idiomatic: Outstanding officials from district magistrate rank upward were presented to the throne for imperial decision.

sentences.zh: 六法處分如京察，貪酷者特參。

translations.literal: Disposition under the six categories was as in the capital inspection; the greedy and cruel were specially impeached.
translations.idiomatic: Disciplinary measures followed the same six categories as the capital inspection, with corrupt and brutal officials specially impeached.

sentences.zh: 凡京察一等、大計卓異有定額，京官七而一，筆帖式八而一，道、府、廳、州、縣十五而一，佐雜、教官百三十而一，以是為率。

translations.literal: First-grade capital inspection and outstanding grand-assessment nominations had fixed quotas: one in seven for capital officials, one in eight for clerks, one in fifteen for circuit, prefectural, subprefectural, department, and county officials, one in one hundred thirty for assistants, clerks, and instructors—such were the ratios.
translations.idiomatic: Quotas governed first-grade capital ratings and outstanding grand-assessment nominations: one in seven for metropolitan officials, one in eight for clerks, one in fifteen for circuit and county-level officers, one in one hundred thirty for assistants and instructors.

sentences.zh: 非歷俸滿者，未及年限者，革職留任或錢糧未完者，滿官不射布靶、不諳清語者，均不得膺上考。

translations.literal: Those who had not completed the full salary term, those not yet at the required tenure, those dismissed but retained or with grain and tax accounts unfinished, and Manchu officials who could not shoot the cloth target or did not know Manchu were all ineligible for top ratings.
translations.idiomatic: Officials who had not completed required tenure, those with incomplete fiscal accounts, those dismissed but retained in post, and Banner officers unable to pass archery or speak Manchu were all barred from top ratings.

sentences.zh: 其大較也。

translations.literal: Such were the general provisions.
translations.idiomatic: Such were the general rules.

sentences.zh: 順治八年，京察始著為令，以六年為期。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Shunzhi, the capital inspection was first established by statute, on a six-year cycle.
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi 8 (1651), the capital inspection was first codified on a six-year cycle.

sentences.zh: 十三年，吏部奏定則例，三品以上自陳，四品等官吏部、都察院察考議奏，親定去留。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year, the Board of Civil Appointments memorialized fixed regulations: third rank and above submitted self-assessments; fourth rank and below were inspected by the Board and the Censorate, deliberated, memorialized, and the emperor personally decided retention or removal.
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi 13 (1656), the Board codified rules: third-rank officials and above submitted self-assessments; fourth-rank and below were examined by the Board and Censorate, with the emperor deciding retention or removal.

sentences.zh: 筆帖式照有職官例一體考察。

translations.literal: Clerks were examined together with regular officials according to the same rules.
translations.idiomatic: Clerks were examined under the same rules as regular officials.

sentences.zh: 遇京察時，各官暫停升轉。

translations.literal: When the capital inspection occurred, all officials temporarily ceased promotion or transfer.
translations.idiomatic: During the capital inspection, promotions and transfers were suspended.

sentences.zh: 尋復定考滿議敘例，三年考滿與六年察典並行。

translations.literal: Soon regulations for consideration upon completion of review were re-established; triennial completion of review and the six-year inspection were conducted in parallel.
translations.idiomatic: Soon rules for triennial review rewards were restored, running the three-year completion review alongside the six-year inspection.

sentences.zh: 十七年，從左都御史魏裔介請，行糾拾之法，以補甄別所未及。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year, following the request of the Left Censor-in-Chief Wei Yijie, the method of supplementary impeachment was instituted to remedy what screening had missed.
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi 17 (1660), at the request of Left Censor-in-Chief Wei Yijie, supplementary impeachment procedures were introduced to catch what regular screening missed.

sentences.zh: 唐熙元年罷京察，專用三年考滿例。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tangxi, the capital inspection was abolished and only the triennial completion review was used.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 1 (1662), the capital inspection was abolished in favor of the triennial completion review alone.

sentences.zh: 三品以上仍自陳。

translations.literal: Third rank and above still submitted self-assessments.
translations.idiomatic: Third-rank officials and above still submitted self-assessments.

sentences.zh: 餘官分五等：一等稱職者紀錄，二等稱職者賞賚，平常者留任，不及者降調，不稱職者革職。

translations.literal: The remaining officials were divided into five grades: first-grade competent ones were recorded; second-grade competent ones received rewards; average ones were retained; those falling short were demoted or transferred; incompetent ones were dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Other officials were graded in five tiers: top competent officials were recorded for promotion; second-tier competent ones received rewards; average ones kept their posts; substandard ones demoted; incompetent ones dismissed.

sentences.zh: 三年，御史季振宜請停考滿三疏，極言徇情鑽營，章奏繁擾，無裨勸懲。

translations.literal: In the third year, Censor Ji Zhenyi memorialized three times to halt the completion review, strongly arguing that favoritism and scheming prevailed, memorials were numerous and disruptive, and it did nothing to encourage or punish.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 3 (1664), Censor Ji Zhenyi submitted three memorials to abolish the completion review, arguing that favoritism and careerism dominated, paperwork overwhelmed the court, and the system failed to reward merit or punish failure.

sentences.zh: 因停考滿自陳例。

translations.literal: Accordingly the practice of self-assessment upon completion of review was halted.
translations.idiomatic: Self-assessment upon completion of review was accordingly abolished.

sentences.zh: 六年，復行京察。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, the capital inspection was restored.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 6 (1667), the capital inspection was restored.

sentences.zh: 明年，甄別不及官三十七員。

translations.literal: The following year, thirty-seven officials who failed screening were identified.
translations.idiomatic: The following year, thirty-seven substandard officials were identified.

sentences.zh: 嗣以各部、院甄別司員，類多末職，二十三年，嚴諭指名題參，復甄汰王三省等三十六人。

translations.literal: Thereafter, as ministries and agencies screened their clerks, most culled were low-ranking posts; in the twenty-third year a stern edict ordered impeachment by name, and thirty-six more including Wang Sansheng were screened out.
translations.idiomatic: Because ministries mostly culled junior staff, Kangxi 23 (1684) brought an edict demanding named impeachments of senior officials; thirty-six more, including Wang Sansheng, were removed.

sentences.zh: 明年，京察又停。

translations.literal: The following year, the capital inspection was again suspended.
translations.idiomatic: The capital inspection was suspended again the next year.

sentences.zh: 雍正元年復舉行，改為三年，自是為定制。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongzheng it was revived, changed to a three-year cycle, and thereafter became the established rule.
translations.idiomatic: It was revived in Yongzheng 1 (1723) on a three-year cycle, which thereafter became standard.

sentences.zh: 初，京察一等無定額，康熙三年，御史張沖翼疏請以部、院員數之多寡定一、二等名數，以息奔競，從之。

translations.literal: At first there was no fixed quota for first-grade capital inspection; in the third year of Kangxi, Censor Zhang Chongyi memorialized that first- and second-grade numbers should be set according to the size of each ministry and agency, to quell scrambling for favor, and this was approved.
translations.idiomatic: Initially first-grade capital ratings had no quota; in Kangxi 3 (1664), Censor Zhang Chongyi proposed fixing first- and second-grade numbers by ministry size to curb favor-seeking, and the court agreed.

sentences.zh: 乾隆間，部、院保送一等，或浮濫溢舊額，詔停兼部行走，仍歸本衙門另班聲敘，暨到任未滿半年，仍由原衙門註考等例。

translations.literal: During the Qianlong reign, when ministries recommended first-grade nominees, nominations sometimes exceeded old quotas; an edict halted concurrent service in other ministries, required separate ranking within one's home office, and provided that those in post less than half a year were still evaluated by their original office.
translations.idiomatic: Under Qianlong, first-grade nominations often exceeded quotas; edicts ended concurrent cross-ministry service, required separate ranking within home offices, and kept officials of less than six months' tenure under their original ministry's evaluation.

sentences.zh: 又罷未授職庶吉士保列一等之例，以示限制。

translations.literal: The practice of recommending unassigned Hanlin bachelors for first grade was also abolished, to show restraint.
translations.idiomatic: Unassigned Hanlin bachelors were also barred from first-grade nomination as a further restriction.

sentences.zh: 四十二年，命部、院保送一等人數，毋庸過泥上屆成例，遞行裁減，以防溢額。

translations.literal: In the forty-second year, ministries and agencies were ordered that first-grade nominations need not rigidly follow the previous session's precedent but should be progressively reduced to prevent exceeding quotas.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 42 (1777), ministries were told not to match previous sessions' first-grade numbers but to reduce nominations progressively to prevent quota inflation.

sentences.zh: 應將上兩次數目比較，酌中定制。

translations.literal: The numbers of the last two sessions should be compared and a moderate standard fixed.
translations.idiomatic: Quotas were to be set by comparing the last two sessions and striking a moderate balance.

sentences.zh: 既無慮濫膺保薦，亦不至屈抑人才。

translations.literal: Thus there was no fear of reckless recommendation, nor of unjustly suppressing talent.
translations.idiomatic: This would curb inflated nominations without unfairly suppressing able officials.

sentences.zh: 五十年，定例保送一等人數，以不溢四十八年原額為準。

translations.literal: In the fiftieth year, it was fixed by regulation that first-grade nominations should not exceed the original quota of the forty-eighth year.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 50 (1785), regulations capped first-grade nominations at the Qianlong 48 quota.

sentences.zh: 後世踵行，間有增損，無甚懸殊也。

translations.literal: Later ages followed suit, with occasional increases or decreases, but no great divergence.
translations.idiomatic: Later reigns followed this practice with minor adjustments but no major change.

sentences.zh: 向例部、院司官由吏部、都察院考覈，雍正四年，命內閣大學士同閱。

translations.literal: By former practice, ministry and agency officials were examined by the Board of Civil Appointments and the Censorate; in the fourth year of Yongzheng, Grand Secretaries of the Grand Secretariat were ordered to review jointly.
translations.idiomatic: Traditionally the Board and Censorate examined ministry staff; in Yongzheng 4 (1726), Grand Secretaries were ordered to review jointly.

sentences.zh: 乾隆九年，帝慮部、院堂官有瞻徇情面濫列一等者，敕大學士驗看，慎重甄別，不稱一等者裁去。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Qianlong, the emperor, fearing that ministry chiefs showed favoritism in listing first-grade nominees, ordered grand ministers to verify, scrutinize carefully, and strike those unworthy of first grade.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 9 (1744), fearing ministry chiefs favored protégés with first-grade ratings, the emperor ordered grand ministers to verify nominations and strike unworthy candidates.

sentences.zh: 十一年諭曰：「前命大學士分別去留，亦權宜辦理之道。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year an edict said: "The earlier order for grand ministers to decide retention or removal was also an expedient measure.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 11 (1746) an edict stated: "Having grand ministers decide retention was only an expedient.

sentences.zh: 察覈司員，惟堂官最為親切。

translations.literal: In examining clerks, only the department chiefs are most intimate with them.
translations.idiomatic: Department chiefs know their staff best and are best placed to evaluate them.

sentences.zh: 要在平日留心體察，臨時舉措公平。

translations.literal: What matters is daily attentive observation and fair action when the time comes.
translations.idiomatic: They should observe staff daily and act fairly at inspection time.

sentences.zh: 如上次定一等者，三年中行走平常，當改為二、三等。

translations.literal: If one rated first grade last time has performed only ordinarily in three years, he should be changed to second or third grade.
translations.idiomatic: Officials rated first grade last time but merely average since should be downgraded to second or third grade.

sentences.zh: 上次原列二、三等者，三年中知所奮勉，即改為一等。

translations.literal: Those previously listed in second or third grade who in three years have shown exertion should be raised to first grade.
translations.idiomatic: Those previously in second or third grade who have improved should be promoted to first grade.

sentences.zh: 庶察典肅而人知勸懲。

translations.literal: Thus the inspection would be rigorous and people would know encouragement and punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Only then would inspections be rigorous and officials know that merit and failure have consequences.

sentences.zh: 」厥後考察權責，悉屬吏部，驗看特奉行故事而已。

translations.literal: "Thereafter examination authority rested entirely with the Board of Civil Appointments; verification became mere observance of precedent.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter examination authority reverted entirely to the Board, and grand-minister verification became a mere formality.

sentences.zh: 大臣循例自陳求斥罷，候旨照舊供職，國初以來行之。

translations.literal: Grand ministers routinely submitted self-assessments asking to be dismissed, awaited edict, and continued in office as before—practiced since the founding of the dynasty.
translations.idiomatic: Since the dynasty's founding, senior ministers had ritually submitted self-assessments requesting dismissal, then continued in office upon imperial leave.

sentences.zh: 乾隆八年，曾諭大臣自陳罷斥者舉賢自代。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Qianlong, an edict once ordered ministers who submitted self-assessments asking dismissal to recommend worthy successors.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 8 (1743), ministers submitting self-dismissal assessments were ordered to recommend worthy successors.

sentences.zh: 嗣以所舉不得其人，或樹黨營私，行不久即罷。

translations.literal: Later, because those recommended were unfit, or formed factions for private gain, the practice was soon abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: The practice was soon dropped because nominees proved unfit or factional, or recommenders were themselves soon dismissed.

sentences.zh: 十七年，帝以「內、外大臣親自簡擢，隨時黜陟，奚待三年？

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year the emperor said: "Inner and outer grand ministers are personally selected and promoted, dismissed or advanced at any time—why wait three years?
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 17 (1752) the emperor declared: "I personally appoint and dismiss inner and outer ministers at will—why wait three years?

sentences.zh: 自陳繁文，相率為偽，甚無謂也」。

translations.literal: Self-assessment is verbose paperwork; all follow one another in hypocrisy—it is quite meaningless."
translations.idiomatic: These self-assessments are empty formalities, universally hypocritical and utterly pointless."

sentences.zh: 詔罷其例。

translations.literal: An edict abolished the practice.
translations.idiomatic: An edict abolished the practice.

sentences.zh: 先是京堂官無甄敘例，乾隆十五年，帝以三品以上堂官，具本自陳，部、院司員，皆令引見，而四、五品京堂不在自陳之列，亦無引見之例，吏部、都察院考語無實，龍鍾庸劣者得姑容，才具優長者無由見。

translations.literal: Previously metropolitan officials of ministerial rank had no evaluation-for-promotion precedent; in the fifteenth year of Qianlong the emperor noted that third-rank and above submitted memorial self-assessments, ministry clerks were all presented, but fourth- and fifth-rank metropolitan officials were neither in the self-assessment list nor presented; Board and Censorate evaluations lacked substance; doddering and mediocre men were tolerated while the talented had no avenue to be seen.
translations.idiomatic: Previously fourth- and fifth-rank metropolitan officials had no promotion review: third-rank and above submitted self-assessments and ministry staff were presented, but fourth- and fifth-rank officials were neither assessed nor presented; Board evaluations were perfunctory, mediocre officials were tolerated, and able ones had no chance to advance.

sentences.zh: 特派王、大臣分別等第，奏聞引見。

translations.literal: Princes and grand ministers were specially dispatched to grade them separately, memorialize, and present them.
translations.idiomatic: Princes and senior ministers were specially assigned to grade them, memorialize, and present them to the throne.

sentences.zh: 十八年，敕吏部開列三品京堂事實，親為裁奪。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year the Board of Civil Appointments was ordered to list the facts on third-rank metropolitan officials for the emperor's personal decision.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 18 (1753) the emperor ordered the Board to submit factual records on third-rank metropolitan officials for his personal decision.

sentences.zh: 四十八年，以三品京堂不便派大臣驗看，令吏部帶額引見。

translations.literal: In the forty-eighth year, because it was inconvenient to assign ministers to verify third-rank metropolitan officials, the Board was ordered to present them within quota.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 48 (1783), third-rank metropolitan officials were presented by the Board within quota rather than by assigned verifying ministers.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶十二年，以三、四品京堂，向來京察但有降黜無甄敘，既與內、外大臣辦理兩歧，並不得與部、院司員同邀加級。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year of Jiaqing, because third- and fourth-rank metropolitan officials in the capital inspection had only demotion without evaluation for promotion—diverging from inner and outer grand ministers and unable to receive rank increments like ministry clerks—
translations.idiomatic: In Jiaqing 12 (1807), because third- and fourth-rank metropolitan officials faced only demotion in the capital inspection, unlike other senior officials and ministry staff who could earn rank increments—

sentences.zh: 於是予太常少卿色克精額等議敘，而予陳鍾琛等休致。

translations.literal: accordingly Vice Minister of Imperial Sacrifices Sekejing'e and others were granted consideration for promotion, while Chen Zhongchen and others were retired.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Minister of Imperial Sacrifices Sekejing'e and others were granted promotion consideration, while Chen Zhongchen and others were retired.

sentences.zh: 自後三品以下京堂始有甄敘之例矣。

translations.literal: From then on metropolitan officials below third rank first had the precedent of evaluation for promotion.
translations.idiomatic: From then on, metropolitan officials below third rank could receive promotion consideration through the capital inspection.

sentences.zh: 年老休致，例有明文。

translations.literal: Retirement on account of age had clear regulations.
translations.idiomatic: Mandatory retirement by age was clearly regulated.

sentences.zh: 乾隆二十二年，定部、院屬官五十五歲以上，堂官詳加甄別。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year of Qianlong, it was fixed that subordinate officials of ministries and agencies aged fifty-five and above should be carefully screened by department chiefs.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 22 (1757), ministry officials aged fifty-five and above were to be carefully screened by their chiefs.

sentences.zh: 三十三年，改定京察二、三等留任各官，六十五歲以上引見。

translations.literal: In the thirty-third year it was revised that officials retained in second or third grade at the capital inspection who were sixty-five and above should be presented.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 33 (1768), second- and third-grade officials retained in post who were sixty-five or older were to be presented to the throne.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶三年，命京察二、三等官引見，以年逾七十為限。

translations.literal: In the third year of Jiaqing, second- and third-grade officials at the capital inspection were ordered presented, with the limit of over seventy years of age.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiaqing 3 (1798), second- and third-grade officials were presented only if over seventy.

sentences.zh: 尋復舊例。

translations.literal: Soon the former rule was restored.
translations.idiomatic: The earlier rule was soon restored.

sentences.zh: 六法處分綦嚴，長官往往博寬大之名，每屆京察，祗黜退數人，虛應故事，餘概優容，而被劾者又不免屈抑。

translations.literal: The six categories of disposition were extremely strict, yet superiors often sought a reputation for leniency; at each capital inspection only a few were dismissed, empty compliance with form, the rest broadly indulged, while the impeached were not spared wrongful suppression.
translations.idiomatic: Though the six disciplinary categories were strict, chiefs often sought reputations for leniency: each inspection dismissed only a few officials as a formality, indulged the rest, yet still wrongfully suppressed those impeached.

sentences.zh: 雍正中，汪景祺、查嗣庭輩論列時政，以部員壅滯為言，有「十年不調、白首為郎」等語。

translations.literal: In the Yongzheng era, Wang Jingqi, Zha Siting, and others discussed current affairs, speaking of congestion among ministry staff, with phrases such as "ten years without transfer, white-haired yet still a gentleman-attendant."
translations.idiomatic: Under Yongzheng, Wang Jingqi, Zha Siting, and others criticized current affairs, citing ministry congestion with lines such as "ten years without promotion, white-haired yet still a gentleman-attendant."

sentences.zh: 帝責以怨望誹謗，而事實不得謂誣。

translations.literal: The emperor rebuked them for resentful slander, yet the facts could not be called false.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor condemned them for seditious slander, though their facts were not false.

sentences.zh: 蓋部員冗濫，康、雍時已然矣。

translations.literal: For ministry staff were redundant and excessive—already so in the Kangxi and Yongzheng eras.
translations.idiomatic: Ministry overstaffing was already a problem under Kangxi and Yongzheng.

sentences.zh: 乾隆三年，鴻臚少卿查斯海疏言：「京官被劾，不無以嫌隙入吏議者。

translations.literal: In the third year of Qianlong, Vice Minister of State Ceremonial Zha Sihai memorialized: "When capital officials are impeached, some enter the Board's deliberation out of personal animosity.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 3 (1738), Vice Minister of State Ceremonial Zha Sihai memorialized: "Impeached capital officials are sometimes punished because of personal grudges.

sentences.zh: 京察六法官，應援大計例送部引見。

translations.literal: Officials under the six categories at the capital inspection should, following the grand-assessment precedent, be sent to the ministry for presentation.
translations.idiomatic: Officials disciplined under the six capital-inspection categories should, as in the grand assessment, be presented to the Board for review.

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: "This was approved.
translations.idiomatic: The proposal was approved.

sentences.zh: 乾隆末，士夫習為諂諛，堂官拔識司員，率以逢迎巧捷為曉事，察典懈弛。

translations.literal: At the end of Qianlong, scholars and officials practiced flattery; department chiefs selected clerks, generally taking ingratiating cleverness as practical sense; the inspection grew lax.
translations.idiomatic: By late Qianlong, flattery prevailed; chiefs favored ingratiating cleverness over competence, and inspections grew lax.

sentences.zh: 仁宗初，銳意求治，頗思以崇實黜華，獎勵氣節，風示天下。

translations.literal: Early in the Jiaqing reign, the emperor was keen to seek good governance and wished to elevate substance over show, encourage integrity, and set an example for the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Jiaqing's reign, the emperor sought good governance, hoping to reward substance over show, encourage integrity, and set an example for the empire.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶五年，詔部、院堂官慎重選舉，猷守兼優者膺首薦，餘寧取資格較久、謹愿樸實之員，其少年浮薄、才華髮越者，應令深其經練，下屆保列。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Jiaqing an edict ordered ministry chiefs to choose carefully: those excellent in both planning and integrity should receive first recommendation; for the rest, prefer those of longer seniority who were cautious and plain; youthful frivolous ones and those of flashy talent should deepen their experience and be recommended in the next session.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiaqing 5 (1800) an edict ordered careful nominations: officials outstanding in both policy and integrity should be recommended first; otherwise prefer senior, steady officials; youthful or flashy talents should gain experience and wait for the next inspection.

sentences.zh: 尚書、侍郎各備冊密識賢否，公議同覽。

translations.literal: Ministers and vice ministers each kept registers secretly noting merit or demerit, for joint review in council.
translations.idiomatic: Ministers and vice ministers were to keep private registers of officials' merit and review them collectively.

sentences.zh: 十一年，大學士、尚書等議奏京察事宜：「捐納人員，限以年資，軍機處司員能兼部務者，方列上考，不許濫保充數。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year, grand ministers and ministers deliberated and memorialized on capital inspection matters: "Purchased-office holders should be limited by seniority; Grand Council clerks able to handle ministry duties may receive top ratings; indiscriminate nomination to fill quotas is forbidden."
translations.idiomatic: In Jiaqing 11 (1806) senior ministers memorialized on the capital inspection: "Purchased offices should be limited by seniority; only Grand Council clerks who also handle ministry work may receive top ratings; padding nominations is forbidden."

sentences.zh: 」報可。

translations.literal: Approval was granted.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was approved.

sentences.zh: 道光四年，候際清贖罪舞弊一案，刑部司員恩德等朋謀撞騙堂官，以謬登薦牘，保列一等，下部議處。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Daoguang, in the case of Hou Jiqing's ransomed punishment and fraud, Ministry of Justice clerks Ende and others conspired in a gang to deceive department chiefs and had them wrongly entered on recommendation lists as first grade; the matter was sent down for deliberation and disposition.
translations.idiomatic: In Daoguang 4 (1824), in the Hou Jiqing bribery case, Ministry of Justice clerks including Ende conspired to deceive their chiefs into recommending unworthy officials for first grade; the case was referred for disciplinary action.

sentences.zh: 諭嗣後京察有冒濫徇私者連坐。

translations.literal: An edict ordered that thereafter in the capital inspection those who recklessly exceeded quotas or showed favoritism would be punished collectively.
translations.idiomatic: An edict decreed collective punishment for future capital inspections marred by favoritism or inflated nominations.

sentences.zh: 七年，給事中吳傑奏：「大計、軍政，皆有舉有劾。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, Supervising Secretary Wu Jie memorialized: "The grand assessment and military inspections all have both recommendation and impeachment.
translations.idiomatic: In Daoguang 7 (1827), Supervising Secretary Wu Jie memorialized: "The grand assessment and military inspections both include commendation and impeachment.

sentences.zh: 近年六部辦理京察，除保舉一等外，不問賢否，概列二等。

translations.literal: In recent years the Six Ministries conducted the capital inspection: apart from recommending first grade, regardless of merit all were listed second grade.
translations.idiomatic: Recently the Six Ministries rated nearly everyone second grade regardless of merit, recommending only a few for first grade.

sentences.zh: 間有三等數人，仍予留任。

translations.literal: Occasionally a few in third grade were still retained in office.
translations.idiomatic: A handful received third grade yet were still retained.

sentences.zh: 六法不施，有勸無懲。

translations.literal: The six categories were not applied; there was encouragement without punishment.
translations.idiomatic: The six disciplinary categories went unused—reward without punishment.

sentences.zh: 應申明舊章，舉劾並用。

translations.literal: The old regulations should be declared and recommendation and impeachment used together.
translations.idiomatic: Old regulations should be enforced so commendation and impeachment work together.

sentences.zh: 」帝韙其言，降諭飭行。

translations.literal: "The emperor approved his words and issued an edict ordering compliance.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed and issued an edict ordering compliance.

sentences.zh: 十五年，令於京察外隨時糾參，以為補救。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year, it was ordered that outside the capital inspection impeachment might occur at any time as a remedy.
translations.idiomatic: In Daoguang 15 (1835), officials could be impeached at any time outside the regular inspection as a corrective measure.

sentences.zh: 咸豐十年，刑部堂官濫保不諳例案之員，朝廷務循寬大，輒以相習成風，不獨刑部為然，多為原宥。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Xianfeng, Ministry of Justice chiefs recklessly recommended staff ignorant of case precedents; the court pursued leniency, and this became habitual—not only in the Ministry of Justice; most were pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: In Xianfeng 10 (1860), Ministry of Justice chiefs recommended officials ignorant of legal precedent; the court's habitual leniency extended across ministries, and most offenders were pardoned.

sentences.zh: 僅予大學士桂良等鐫級留任，出考堂官罰俸而已。

translations.literal: Only Grand Secretary Gui Liang and others had a rank inscription removed but were retained; the chiefs who conducted the inspection were merely fined.
translations.idiomatic: Only Grand Secretary Gui Liang and others lost a rank increment while retaining office; inspecting chiefs received only salary fines.

sentences.zh: 穆宗即位，大難未平，厲精澄敘。

translations.literal: When the Muzong emperor acceded, great calamity was not yet settled, yet he strove to clarify evaluation.
translations.idiomatic: When the Tongzhi Emperor acceded amid ongoing crisis, he strove to tighten official evaluation.

sentences.zh: 同治五年，詔部、院堂官謹遵嘉慶五年備冊密識賢否、公議同覽之諭，並常川進署，與司員講求公事，藉覘其屬賢否。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Tongzhi an edict ordered ministry chiefs strictly to follow the Jiaqing fifth-year instruction on keeping registers secretly noting merit, joint review, and regularly attending office to discuss public business with clerks, thereby observing subordinates' merit.
translations.idiomatic: In Tongzhi 5 (1866) an edict ordered ministry chiefs to follow Jiaqing's private merit registers and collective review, attend office regularly, discuss business with staff, and thereby assess subordinates.

sentences.zh: 八年，又諭京察不得有舉無劾，冀湔滌舊習，一新庶政。

translations.literal: In the eighth year another edict stated that the capital inspection must not have recommendation without impeachment, hoping to wash away old habits and renew common governance.
translations.idiomatic: In Tongzhi 8 (1869) another edict required both commendation and impeachment in the capital inspection, hoping to break old habits and renew governance.

sentences.zh: 然積重之勢，不能復返。

translations.literal: Yet the weight of accumulated custom could not be reversed.
translations.idiomatic: Yet entrenched habits could not be reversed.

sentences.zh: 光緒七年，禮部侍郎寶廷疏陳京察積弊，言之痛切，謂：「瞻徇情面之弊，不專在部、院堂官，當責樞臣考察，必公必嚴。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Guangxu, Vice Minister of Rites Baoting memorialized on accumulated abuses in the capital inspection, speaking with painful urgency, saying: "The abuse of showing favoritism lies not only with ministry chiefs; the Grand Council ministers should be charged with inspection, which must be fair and strict.
translations.idiomatic: In Guangxu 7 (1881), Vice Minister of Rites Baoting memorialized on capital-inspection abuses, arguing forcefully that favoritism was not limited to ministry chiefs: Grand Council ministers must conduct inspections that were fair and strict.

sentences.zh: 樞臣果精白乃心，破除情面，不特能考察部、院司員之賢否，並能考察內、外大臣之賢否。

translations.literal: If the Grand Council ministers truly purify their hearts and break through favoritism, they can not only inspect the merit of ministry clerks but also inspect inner and outer grand ministers.
translations.idiomatic: If council ministers were truly impartial and broke with favoritism, they could evaluate not only ministry staff but also all senior civil and military officials.

sentences.zh: 而考察樞臣功過，在聖明獨斷。

translations.literal: As for inspecting the achievements and faults of council ministers, that rests in the sage emperor's sole decision.
translations.idiomatic: Judging the council ministers themselves, however, rested with the emperor alone.

sentences.zh: 若朝廷先以京察為故事具文，何責乎樞臣，更何責乎部、院堂官！

translations.literal: If the court first treats the capital inspection as empty precedent, how can one blame council ministers, much less ministry chiefs!
translations.idiomatic: If the court treated the capital inspection as empty formality, how could one blame council ministers—or ministry chiefs?

sentences.zh: 」論雖切中而難實行，徒託空言而已。

translations.literal: "Though the argument hit the mark, it was hard to implement—mere empty words.
translations.idiomatic: His argument was sound but impracticable—mere empty rhetoric.

sentences.zh: 宣統二年，吏部設立憲政籌備處，改考功司為考績科，主文職功過應行變通事宜。

translations.literal: In the second year of Xuantong, the Board of Civil Appointments established a Constitutional Preparation Office, changed the Department of Merit Records to the Performance Evaluation Section, and oversaw matters of reward and punishment for civil officials requiring reform.
translations.idiomatic: In Xuantong 2 (1910), the Board established a Constitutional Preparation Office, renamed the Department of Merit Records the Performance Evaluation Section, and oversaw reforms to civil performance review.

sentences.zh: 其時浮議紛紜，新舊雜糅，吏部等於贅疣矣。

translations.literal: At that time floating opinions were numerous, old and new mixed together, and the Board of Civil Appointments was like a superfluous growth.
translations.idiomatic: By then debate swirled, old and new systems overlapped, and the Board had become largely redundant.

sentences.zh: 大計始順治二年，御史張濩疏請有司殿最，宜以守己端潔、實心愛民為上考。

translations.literal: The grand assessment began in the second year of Shunzhi; Censor Zhang Pu memorialized that in ranking local officials, integrity in self-conduct and sincere love for the people should count as top rating.
translations.idiomatic: The grand assessment began in Shunzhi 2 (1645), when Censor Zhang Pu proposed ranking local officials chiefly on personal integrity and genuine care for the people.

sentences.zh: 部覆如議。

translations.literal: The ministry replied in accord with the proposal.
translations.idiomatic: The Board approved the proposal.

sentences.zh: 明年，定朝覲考察，頒五花冊，令督、撫以四格註考。

translations.literal: The following year, court-audience inspection was fixed; five-pattern registers were issued, ordering governors-general and governors to note evaluations according to four criteria.
translations.idiomatic: The next year court-audience inspection was codified; five-pattern registers were issued, and governors-general and governors were to evaluate officials by four criteria.

sentences.zh: 故事，計參外，台、省例有拾遺。

translations.literal: By precedent, apart from assessment participation, the censorate routinely had supplementary impeachment.
translations.idiomatic: By precedent, besides the formal assessment, censors could also submit supplementary impeachments.

sentences.zh: 是歲計群吏，止據撫、按所揭為黜陟。

translations.literal: That year in assessing all officials, only what governors and surveillance commissioners exposed was used for promotion or demotion.
translations.idiomatic: That year promotions and demotions relied solely on reports from governors and surveillance commissioners.

sentences.zh: 台、省擬循故事，內大臣不喜。

translations.literal: The censorate proposed to follow precedent; inner grand ministers were displeased.
translations.idiomatic: The censorate proposed following precedent, but senior ministers objected.

sentences.zh: 大學士陳名夏力主之，給事中魏象樞亦以為請。

translations.literal: Grand Secretary Chen Mingxia strongly upheld it; Supervising Secretary Wei Xiangdong also requested it.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Secretary Chen Mingxia strongly supported it, as did Supervising Secretary Wei Xiangdong.

sentences.zh: 得旨，糾拾官照大計處分挾私妄糾者論。

translations.literal: An edict was received: impeaching officials who, following grand-assessment disposition, impeached falsely out of private motive would be punished.
translations.idiomatic: An edict decreed punishment for censors who filed false impeachments out of private motive during the grand assessment.

sentences.zh: 自後台、省意存瞻顧，糾拾者鮮。

translations.literal: Thereafter the censorate minded favor and consideration; supplementary impeachers were few.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter the censorate grew cautious, and supplementary impeachments became rare.

sentences.zh: 已，罷不行，而督、撫權乃日重矣。

translations.literal: Soon it was abolished and not implemented, while the power of governors-general and governors grew daily heavier.
translations.idiomatic: The practice was soon abolished, and gubernatorial power grew steadily heavier.

sentences.zh: 四年，定大計三年一舉，計處官不許還職。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, the grand assessment was fixed every three years; officials under assessment were not permitted to return to duty.
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi 4 (1647), the grand assessment was fixed at three-year intervals; officials under review could not resume duty.

sentences.zh: 諭朝覲官曰：「貪酷重懲，闒茸罔貰。

translations.literal: Officials attending court audience were instructed: "The greedy and cruel shall be heavily punished; the incompetent shall not be pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: Officials attending court audience were told: "The greedy and cruel will be severely punished; the incompetent will not be pardoned.

sentences.zh: 爾等姑許留任，當思祓濯前愆，勉圖後效。

translations.literal: You are for now permitted to remain in office; you should think to cleanse past faults and strive for future achievement."
translations.idiomatic: You are temporarily retained in office; cleanse past faults and strive to do better."

sentences.zh: 」嗣是每屆入覲之年，必嚴切誡飭以為常。

translations.literal: Thereafter, every year of court audience, stern admonition became the rule.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter stern admonitions became routine in every court-audience year.

sentences.zh: 舊例朝覲計典，籓、臬、府、州、縣正官皆入覲。

translations.literal: By old rule in the court-audience assessment, provincial, judicial, prefectural, department, and county chief officials all attended court.
translations.idiomatic: By old rule, provincial, judicial, prefectural, and county chiefs all attended court for the assessment.

sentences.zh: 順治九年，止令籓、臬各一員、各府佐一員代覲。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Shunzhi, only one provincial and one judicial official each, and one assistant per prefecture, were ordered to attend in proxy.
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi 9 (1652), only one provincial and one judicial officer each, plus one prefectural deputy per prefecture, attended in proxy.

sentences.zh: 十八年，給事中雷一龍疏言；

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year, Supervising Secretary Lei Yilong memorialized:
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi 18 (1661), Supervising Secretary Lei Yilong memorialized:

sentences.zh: 「三年大計，勿得遺大吏而摘微員，懲去位而寬現在。

translations.literal: "In the triennial grand assessment, do not overlook great officials while picking at minor ones, punish those who have left office while indulging those now in post.
translations.idiomatic: "In the triennial grand assessment, do not overlook senior officials while punishing only minor ones, or punish departed officials while indulging those still in office.

sentences.zh: 請令籓、臬赴部，面同指實，按冊詳察。

translations.literal: Request that provincial and judicial officials come to the ministry, face-to-face verify facts, and examine in detail according to the registers."
translations.idiomatic: Require provincial and judicial officials to come to the capital, verify facts in person, and examine registers in detail."

sentences.zh: 」下部議行。

translations.literal: The matter was sent to the ministry for deliberation and implementation.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was referred to the Board for implementation.

sentences.zh: 康熙元年，停籓、臬入覲，以參政、副使等官代。

translations.literal: In the first year of Kangxi, provincial and judicial attendance at court was halted; administrative commissioners, vice commissioners, and others attended in their place.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 1 (1662), provincial and judicial chiefs ceased attending court; administrative commissioners and vice commissioners attended instead.

sentences.zh: 十二年，復令籓、臬入覲。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year, provincial and judicial officials were again ordered to attend court.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 12 (1673), provincial and judicial chiefs were again required to attend court.

sentences.zh: 二十五年，以朝覲藉端苛派，奸弊滋生，籓、臬、府佐入覲例悉罷。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year, because court audience was used as a pretext for harsh levies and abuses flourished, the rules for provincial, judicial, and prefectural deputies to attend court were all abolished.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 25 (1686), because court audience became a pretext for extortion and corruption, all rules requiring provincial, judicial, and prefectural deputies to attend were abolished.

sentences.zh: 官吏賢否去留，憑督、撫文冊，布、按二司冊籍悉停止。

translations.literal: Whether officials were worthy, retained, or removed depended on governors' written registers; the registers of the provincial administration and surveillance commissions were all discontinued.
translations.idiomatic: Officials' merit and retention depended on governors' reports alone; registers from the provincial administration and surveillance commissions were discontinued.

sentences.zh: 國初大計與考滿並行，康熙元年，罷大計，止行考滿。

translations.literal: At the founding of the dynasty the grand assessment and completion-of-review ran in parallel; in the first year of Kangxi the grand assessment was abolished and only completion of review was conducted.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the dynasty the grand assessment ran alongside triennial completion review; in Kangxi 1 the grand assessment was abolished in favor of completion review alone.

sentences.zh: 司、道歷腹俸二年、邊俸一年半，有司歷邊俸二年、腹俸三年，錢糧全完者許考滿。

translations.literal: Circuit intendants and commissioners served two years on interior salary and one and a half on frontier salary; local officials served two years on frontier salary and three on interior salary; those who completed grain and tax accounts in full were permitted completion of review.
translations.idiomatic: Circuit officials needed two years on interior salary and one and a half on frontier salary; local officials needed two years on frontier salary and three on interior salary; only those with complete fiscal accounts could complete review.

sentences.zh: 分別地方荒殘、沖疲、充實、簡易四者開註，以政績多寡酌定等第。

translations.literal: Places were distinguished as devastated, heavily burdened, prosperous, or simple, and noted accordingly; grades were adjusted according to the amount of administrative achievement.
translations.idiomatic: Localities were classified as devastated, overburdened, prosperous, or simple, and grades were adjusted according to administrative achievement.

sentences.zh: 四年，考滿停，復行大計，為永制。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, completion of review was halted and the grand assessment was restored as permanent rule.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 4 (1665), completion review was halted and the grand assessment was permanently restored.

sentences.zh: 大計舉劾註考，例由州、縣正官申送本府、道考覈；

translations.literal: For grand-assessment recommendation, impeachment, and evaluation, by rule district and county chiefs submitted upward to prefecture and circuit for examination;
translations.idiomatic: Grand-assessment nominations, impeachments, and evaluations normally began with district and county chiefs submitting upward to prefecture and circuit for review;

sentences.zh: 教官由學道，鹽政官由該正官考覈；

translations.literal: instructors were examined by the educational circuit; salt administration officials by their supervising chief;
translations.idiomatic: instructors were examined by the educational intendant; salt officials by their supervising chief;

sentences.zh: 轉呈布、按覆考，督、撫覈定，咨達部、院。

translations.literal: reports were forwarded to provincial administration and surveillance for re-examination, governors-general and governors verified and finalized, and the matter was communicated to ministries and agencies.
translations.idiomatic: then forwarded to provincial administration and surveillance for re-examination, finalized by governors-general and governors, and reported to the ministries.

sentences.zh: 河官兼有刑名、錢糧之責者，總河、督、撫各行考覈。

translations.literal: River officials who also bore responsibility for judicial and fiscal matters were examined separately by the director-general of rivers, governors-general, and governors.
translations.idiomatic: River officials with judicial and fiscal duties were examined separately by the director-general of rivers and by governors.

sentences.zh: 專管河務者，總河自行考覈具題。

translations.literal: Those who managed river works exclusively were examined by the director-general himself and memorialized.
translations.idiomatic: Officials managing river works exclusively were examined and memorialized by the director-general alone.

sentences.zh: 康熙二十三年，以籓、臬與督、撫親近，停其卓異。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year of Kangxi, because provincial and judicial officials were close to governors-general and governors, their outstanding nominations were halted.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 23 (1684), outstanding nominations for provincial and judicial officials were halted because they were too close to governors.

sentences.zh: 凡卓異官紀錄即升，不次擢用。

translations.literal: All outstanding officials were recorded and immediately promoted, appointed out of turn.
translations.idiomatic: Outstanding officials were recorded for immediate promotion, often out of turn.

sentences.zh: 歷朝最重其選，徇私濫保者罪之。

translations.literal: Successive dynasties most valued this selection; those who showed favoritism in reckless recommendation were punished.
translations.idiomatic: Every dynasty prized this selection, and favoritism in nominations was punished.

sentences.zh: 康熙初，御史張沖翼請申嚴卓異定額，以詳覈事迹，使名實相副為言。

translations.literal: Early in Kangxi, Censor Zhang Chongyi requested strict enforcement of outstanding quotas, detailed verification of facts, and that name and reality should match.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Kangxi, Censor Zhang Chongyi urged strict outstanding quotas, detailed verification of records, and matching reputation to reality.

sentences.zh: 下部議。

translations.literal: The matter was sent to the ministry for deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was referred to the Board.

sentences.zh: 六年，從御史田六善請，卓異官以清廉為本，司、道等官必註明不派節禮、索餽送，州、縣等官必註明不派雜差、重火耗、虧損行戶、強貸富民。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, following Censor Tian Liushan's request, outstanding officials were to take integrity as foundation; circuit and commissioner officials must note that they did not assign festival gifts or demand supply deliveries; prefectural and county officials must note that they did not assign miscellaneous corvée, impose heavy meltage fees, harm merchants, or force loans on the wealthy.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 6 (1667), following Censor Tian Liushan, outstanding officials had to be fundamentally honest: circuit officials had to certify they took no festival gifts or supply levies; county officials had to certify they imposed no illegal corvée, excessive meltage fees, merchant losses, or forced loans on the wealthy.

sentences.zh: 以清吏之有無，定督、撫之賢否。

translations.literal: Whether subordinates were honest determined whether governors were worthy.
translations.idiomatic: Governors' merit was judged by whether their subordinates were honest.

sentences.zh: 其時廉吏輩出，靈壽令陸隴其等擢隸憲府，吏治蒸蒸，稱極盛焉。

translations.literal: At that time honest officials emerged in succession; Ling Shou magistrate Lu Longqi and others were promoted to judicial posts; administration flourished, called the greatest prosperity.
translations.idiomatic: Honest officials flourished; Magistrate Lu Longqi of Lingshou and others were promoted to judicial posts, and local administration reached its zenith.

sentences.zh: 四十四年，詔舉卓異，務期無加派，無濫刑，無盜案，無錢糧拖久、倉庫虧空，民生得所，地方日有起色。

translations.literal: In the forty-fourth year an edict ordered outstanding nominations, requiring no extra levies, no abusive punishment, no bandit cases, no prolonged grain and tax arrears or granary deficits, the people's livelihood settled, and the locality daily improving.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 44 (1705) an edict required outstanding nominations only for officials with no extra levies, abusive punishments, bandit cases, fiscal arrears, granary deficits, and with improving livelihoods and local conditions.

sentences.zh: 其他虛文，不必開載。

translations.literal: Other empty verbiage need not be entered.
translations.idiomatic: Empty formalities need not be recorded.

sentences.zh: 乾隆八年，命督、撫以務農本計察覈屬員，論者謂以勸農為勸吏之要，深得治本，與漢詔同風。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Qianlong, governors-general and governors were ordered to examine subordinates with promotion of agriculture as fundamental policy; commentators said that taking encouragement of farming as the key to encouraging officials deeply grasped governing the root, in the same spirit as Han edicts.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 8 (1743), governors were ordered to evaluate subordinates on agricultural policy; commentators praised this as grasping the root of governance, in the spirit of Han dynasty edicts.

sentences.zh: 先是雍正六年，定卓異薦舉失實處分，自行奏參者免。

translations.literal: Earlier, in the sixth year of Yongzheng, disposition was fixed for false outstanding recommendations; those who reported themselves were exempted.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, in Yongzheng 6 (1728), penalties were set for false outstanding nominations, with exemption for self-reporting.

sentences.zh: 卓異官有貪酷不法，或錢糧、盜案未清，發覺者，原薦督、撫處分較司、道、府為輕。

translations.literal: When outstanding officials proved greedy, cruel, or lawless, or had uncleared grain, tax, or bandit cases, the recommending governor was punished more lightly than circuit, commissioner, or prefectural officials.
translations.idiomatic: When nominated outstanding officials proved corrupt or had uncleared fiscal or bandit cases, recommending governors were punished more lightly than circuit, commissioner, or prefectural officials.

sentences.zh: 乾隆四十八年，改定卓異官犯贓，覈其年月在原薦上司離任前後，分別議處。

translations.literal: In the forty-eighth year of Qianlong it was revised that when outstanding officials committed corruption, the date relative to their recommender's departure from office should be verified and disposition made accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 48 (1783), when outstanding officials were found corrupt, penalties for their recommenders depended on whether the offense occurred before or after the recommender left office.

sentences.zh: 臬司、道、府減督、撫一等，籓司照督、撫例，以道、府按例轉詳督、撫、籓司親為覈定也。

translations.literal: Surveillance commissioners, circuit officials, and prefects received one grade lighter punishment than governors; provincial administration commissioners followed governors' precedent, because circuit and prefectural officials reported through routine channels for governors, provincial administration commissioners, and surveillance commissioners to verify personally.
translations.idiomatic: Surveillance commissioners, circuit officials, and prefects were punished one grade less than governors; provincial administration commissioners followed governors' precedent, since circuit and prefectural officials reported through them for governors' personal verification.

sentences.zh: 五十年，帝以保薦卓異，向分正附，未明定限制，易開徼幸之漸。

translations.literal: In the fiftieth year the emperor noted that in recommending outstanding officials, primary and supplementary nominations were distinguished but limits were not clearly fixed, easily opening the way to opportunism.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 50 (1785) the emperor noted that primary and supplementary outstanding nominations lacked clear limits, encouraging opportunism.

sentences.zh: 敕部詳覈各省大小、缺分多寡，酌中定制，裁去附薦名目。

translations.literal: The ministry was ordered to examine carefully the size and number of posts in each province, fix a moderate standard, and abolish supplementary nomination titles.
translations.idiomatic: The Board was ordered to calculate provincial post numbers, set moderate quotas, and abolish supplementary nominations.

sentences.zh: 於是各省卓異官有定額，終清世無大變更也。

translations.literal: Thus each province had fixed outstanding quotas, with no great change through the Qing.
translations.idiomatic: Each province then had fixed outstanding quotas, which changed little for the rest of the dynasty.

sentences.zh: 八法處分，行之既久，長吏或視為具文，每將微員細故，填註塞責。

translations.literal: The eight categories of disposition, long in practice, were sometimes treated as empty form by superiors, who filled in minor details of low officials to meet obligation.
translations.idiomatic: The eight disciplinary categories, long in force, were often treated as empty form, with chiefs padding evaluations with minor details about junior staff.

sentences.zh: 歷朝訓諭諄諄，力戒瞻徇，猶防冤抑。

translations.literal: Successive dynasties admonished earnestly, strictly forbidding favoritism, yet still guarding against wrongful suppression.
translations.idiomatic: Successive dynasties earnestly warned against favoritism while also guarding against wrongful suppression.

sentences.zh: 雍正元年，詔大計降級罰俸官，例不許卓異，果有居官廉幹因公詿誤者，淮與卓異。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongzheng an edict stated that officials demoted or fined at the grand assessment were by rule not permitted outstanding nomination, but if truly honest and capable yet wronged by public duty, they might receive outstanding nomination.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongzheng 1 (1723) an edict barred demoted or fined officials from outstanding nomination, except honest capable officials wronged by official duty.

sentences.zh: 又以卓異八法舉劾不過數十人，其不列舉劾之平等官，自知縣以上，令督、撫註考，報部察核。

translations.literal: Also, since outstanding nominations and eight-category impeachment involved only several tens of people, average officials from district magistrates upward who were neither recommended nor impeached were ordered evaluated by governors and reported to the ministry for review.
translations.idiomatic: Because outstanding nominations and eight-category impeachments involved only dozens of officials, governors were also to evaluate average officials from district magistrate rank upward and report to the Board.

sentences.zh: 四年，諭參劾人員或有冤抑及避重就輕等弊，除貪酷官無庸引見外，其不謹、浮躁、不及等被劾官，督、撫給咨送部引見。

translations.literal: In the fourth year an edict stated that impeached persons might suffer wrongful suppression or the abuse of avoiding serious charges for light ones; apart from greedy and cruel officials who need not be presented, those impeached as careless, frivolous, or inadequate should be given credentials by governors and sent to the ministry for presentation.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongzheng 4 (1726) an edict noted wrongful suppression and lenient treatment of serious offenses; except corrupt officials, those impeached as careless, frivolous, or inadequate were to be presented to the Board for review.

sentences.zh: 乾隆二十四年，帝以八法參本內不謹、浮躁官，未將何事不謹、何事浮躁、一一聲敘，或有公事無誤而節目闊疏，才具有為而氣質粗率，上司以意見不洽，概登白簡，不無可惜。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year of Qianlong the emperor noted that in eight-category impeachment memorials, careless and frivolous officials did not have what acts were careless or frivolous stated one by one; some had no error in public business but were loose in procedure, some had capacity but coarse temperament, some were listed wholesale because superiors' views did not agree—it was not without regret.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 24 (1759) the emperor noted that careless and frivolous impeachments often lacked specifics; some capable officials were impeached for procedural looseness or coarse manner, or because superiors disliked them—wasteful of talent.

sentences.zh: 其或敗檢逾閒，僅與避重就輕，均非整飭官方之意。

translations.literal: Or moral failure and excess might receive only lenient treatment, avoiding serious for light charges—all contrary to the intent of rectifying officialdom.
translations.idiomatic: Serious moral failures treated leniently were equally contrary to rectifying official conduct.

sentences.zh: 命詳註實跡，不得籠統參劾。

translations.literal: Detailed factual records were ordered; vague impeachment was forbidden.
translations.idiomatic: Detailed factual records were required; vague impeachments were forbidden.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶八年，定督、撫隨時參劾闒冗平庸等事，未列敘寶跡，被劾官情原赴部引見者，得援大計六法例。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Jiaqing it was fixed that when governors impeached at any time for incompetence, mediocrity, and the like without listing detailed facts, if the impeached official wished to go to the ministry for presentation, the grand-assessment six-category precedent might be invoked.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiaqing 8 (1803), officials impeached at any time for mediocrity without detailed facts could request presentation to the Board under the grand-assessment six-category precedent.

sentences.zh: 此則考覈不厭詳密，冀搜求遺才，輔計典之不及也。

translations.literal: This showed that examination did not tire of detail, hoping to seek overlooked talent and supplement what the assessment ritual could not reach.
translations.idiomatic: This reflected exhaustive review hoping to find overlooked talent beyond what formal assessments could reach.

sentences.zh: 嘉、道以後，計典一循舊例，督、撫奉行故事，鮮克振刷。

translations.literal: After Jiaqing and Daoguang, the assessment ritual followed old precedent; governors observed form, rarely able to revive and reform.
translations.idiomatic: After Jiaqing and Daoguang, assessments followed old precedent; governors observed form but rarely reformed.

sentences.zh: 道光八年，山東大計卓異，護撫賀長齡原註新城令容昺悃愊慈祥等語，詔以寬厚難膺上考，令各省薦舉體用兼備、熟明治理者。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Daoguang, in Shandong's grand assessment outstanding nomination, Acting Governor He Changling originally noted Xincheng magistrate Rong Bing as sincere, kind, and benevolent; an edict held that mere lenience could not qualify for top rating, ordering each province to recommend those combining substance and function who were skilled in governance.
translations.idiomatic: In Daoguang 8 (1828), Acting Governor He Changling of Shandong nominated Magistrate Rong Bing of Xincheng as sincere and benevolent; an edict ruled that lenience alone did not qualify for top rating and ordered nominations of officials skilled in practical governance.

sentences.zh: 咸、同軍興，或地方甫收復，有待撫綏，或疆圉偪寇氛，亟籌保衛，敕各督、撫留心存記廉能之員，列上考，備擢用。

translations.literal: During the Xianfeng and Tongzhi military campaigns, some places had just been recovered and awaited pacification, some frontiers faced bandit threat and urgently needed defense; each governor was ordered to note honest and capable men, list them for top rating, and prepare them for promotion.
translations.idiomatic: During the Xianfeng and Tongzhi wars, some regions needed pacification and others faced bandit threats; governors were ordered to note honest capable officials for top ratings and promotion.

sentences.zh: 時督、撫權宜行事，用人不拘資格，隨時舉措，固不能以大計常例繩其後也。

translations.literal: At that time governors acted expediently, employing men without regard to qualifications, taking measures as needed—they could not be bound afterward by grand-assessment routine.
translations.idiomatic: Governors then acted expediently, appointing without regard to seniority; normal grand-assessment rules could not bind them afterward.

sentences.zh: 光緒間，言者每條奏計典積弊，請飭疆臣認真考察。

translations.literal: During Guangxu, memorialists often itemized accumulated abuses of the assessment ritual and requested that frontier ministers conduct examination earnestly.
translations.idiomatic: Under Guangxu, memorialists repeatedly listed assessment abuses and urged frontier governors to conduct earnest reviews.

sentences.zh: 屢詔戒飭。

translations.literal: Edicts admonished repeatedly.
translations.idiomatic: Repeated edicts admonished them.

sentences.zh: 然人才既衰，吏治日壞，徒法終不能行。

translations.literal: Yet talent had declined and administration worsened daily; mere law in the end could not be enforced.
translations.idiomatic: Yet talent had declined and administration worsened; laws alone could not restore order.

sentences.zh: 二十八年，詔各省設立課吏館，限半年具奏一次。

translations.literal: In the twenty-eighth year an edict ordered each province to establish an official evaluation academy, reporting once every half year.
translations.idiomatic: In Guangxu 28 (1902) an edict ordered each province to establish an official evaluation academy reporting every six months.

sentences.zh: 三十一年，定考覈州、縣事實，分最優等、優等、平等、次等四級。

translations.literal: In the thirty-first year evaluation of prefectural and county facts was fixed, divided into four grades: highest excellent, excellent, average, and substandard.
translations.idiomatic: In Guangxu 31 (1905) prefectural and county evaluations were divided into four grades: highest excellent, excellent, average, and substandard.

sentences.zh: 顧課吏祗憑一日文字，考覈僅據一年事實，責以公當，蓋亦難矣。

translations.literal: Yet official evaluation relied only on one day's writing; assessment used only one year's facts—to demand fairness was indeed difficult.
translations.idiomatic: Yet evaluation relied on a single day's writing and assessment on a single year's record—fair judgment was nearly impossible.

sentences.zh: 宣統二年，憲政編查館疏請考覈州、縣，分別學堂、巡警、工藝、種植、命盜、詞訟、監押、錢漕，以為殿最。

translations.literal: In the second year of Xuantong the Constitutional Compilation and Investigation Office memorialized requesting evaluation of prefectures and counties by schools, police, crafts, planting, homicides and theft, lawsuits, detention, and grain transport as criteria for ranking.
translations.idiomatic: In Xuantong 2 (1910) the Constitutional Compilation Office proposed evaluating prefectures and counties on schools, police, crafts, agriculture, homicides and theft, lawsuits, detention, and grain transport.

sentences.zh: 由主管衙門另訂考覈章程。

translations.literal: Supervising offices were to draw up separate evaluation regulations.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising offices were to draft separate evaluation regulations.

sentences.zh: 名目繁多，表冊虛偽，徒飾耳目，於勸懲無當也。

translations.literal: Categories were numerous, forms and registers false, merely ornament for the eyes, of no use for encouragement or punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Categories multiplied, forms were falsified, and the system served only appearances, not reward or punishment.

sentences.zh: 至若舊例翰、詹大考，分別優劣，升調降革有差，為特別考績之法。

translations.literal: As for the old rule of the Hanlin and Court of Imperial Entertainments great examination, distinguishing excellence and inferiority with differences in promotion, transfer, demotion, and dismissal—it was a special performance-evaluation method.
translations.idiomatic: The Hanlin and Court of Imperial Entertainments great examination, distinguishing excellence with differentiated promotion, transfer, demotion, and dismissal, was a separate evaluation method.

sentences.zh: 外省司、道，年終有密考。

translations.literal: For circuit commissioners and intendants in the provinces, there was confidential year-end examination.
translations.idiomatic: Provincial circuit commissioners and intendants received confidential year-end evaluations.

sentences.zh: 州、縣一年期滿，教、佐六年俸滿，皆有甄別。

translations.literal: Prefectures and counties at one-year term completion, instructors and assistants at six-year salary completion—all had screening.
translations.idiomatic: Prefectural and county officials at one-year completion, instructors and assistants at six-year salary completion—all underwent screening.

sentences.zh: 則又隨時考核之法，不屬於察、計二典者。

translations.literal: These were methods of assessment at any time, not belonging to the two rituals of inspection and grand assessment.
translations.idiomatic: These were ongoing evaluation methods outside the capital inspection and grand assessment.

sentences.zh: 武之軍政，猶文之考察，兵部職方司掌之。

translations.literal: Military inspection was to civil examination as the Board of War's Department of Military Appointments administered it.
translations.idiomatic: Military inspection paralleled civil performance review and was administered by the Board of War's Department of Military Appointments.

sentences.zh: 內、外衛、所，分屬於武選司。

translations.literal: Inner and outer guards and posts fell under the Department of Military Selection.
translations.idiomatic: Inner and outer guards and posts fell under the Department of Military Selection.

sentences.zh: 在京武職，由管旗及部、院覈奏；

translations.literal: Capital military posts were examined and memorialized by banner commanders and ministries;
translations.idiomatic: Capital military officials were examined and memorialized by banner commanders and ministries;

sentences.zh: 各省由統兵大員註考。

translations.literal: in the provinces by commanders-in-chief who noted evaluations.
translations.idiomatic: provincial ones by commanders-in-chief who recorded evaluations.

sentences.zh: 京營千總以上，外省綠營守備以上，各由長官考覈，分操守、才能、騎射、年歲四格。

translations.literal: Capital garrison battalion commanders and above, provincial Green Standard garrison commanders and above, were each examined by superiors, divided into four criteria: integrity, ability, horsemanship and archery, and age.
translations.idiomatic: Capital garrison battalion commanders and provincial Green Standard garrison commanders and above were examined by superiors on integrity, ability, horsemanship and archery, and age.

sentences.zh: 舉劾與文職同。

translations.literal: Recommendation and impeachment were the same as for civil officials.
translations.idiomatic: Commendation and impeachment followed the same rules as for civil officials.

sentences.zh: 三品以上自陳，由部疏聞候旨。

translations.literal: Third rank and above submitted self-assessments; the ministry memorialized and awaited imperial decree.
translations.idiomatic: Third-rank officers and above submitted self-assessments; the Board memorialized and awaited imperial decree.

sentences.zh: 八旗世爵，則校其藝進退之。

translations.literal: Hereditary Banner ranks were advanced or retired according to examination of their skills.
translations.idiomatic: Hereditary Banner ranks were advanced or retired according to skill examinations.

sentences.zh: 綠營舉劾，每于軍政後一年半舉行，題升一二人入薦舉班升用，劾者照軍政處分。

translations.literal: Green Standard recommendation and impeachment were held a year and a half after each military inspection; one or two were nominated for promotion into the recommendation roster; impeached ones were disposed of as in military inspection.
translations.idiomatic: Green Standard commendations and impeachments occurred a year and a half after each military inspection; one or two officers were nominated for promotion; impeached officers were disciplined under military-inspection rules.

sentences.zh: 此其大略也。

translations.literal: Such were the general provisions.
translations.idiomatic: Such were the general rules.

sentences.zh: 國初未立限制，順治九年，定六年一舉，是為軍政考覈之始。

translations.literal: At the founding no limit was set; in the ninth year of Shunzhi a six-year cycle was fixed—this was the beginning of military inspection examination.
translations.idiomatic: Initially no cycle was fixed; in Shunzhi 9 (1652) a six-year military inspection was established.

sentences.zh: 十一年，改定五年為期。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year it was changed to a five-year cycle.
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi 11 (1654) the cycle was changed to five years.

sentences.zh: 十三年，從給事中張文光請，軍政卓異，照文官賜服旌勸，後改為加一級。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year, following Supervising Secretary Zhang Wenguang's request, outstanding military inspection nominees, like civil officials, received ceremonial robes and commendation; later this was changed to one rank increment.
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi 13 (1656), following Supervising Secretary Zhang Wenguang, outstanding military nominees received ceremonial rewards like civil officials; later this became a one-rank increment.

sentences.zh: 康熙元年，停軍政，專行考滿。

translations.literal: In the first year of Kangxi, military inspection was halted and only completion of review was conducted.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 1 (1662), military inspection was halted in favor of completion review alone.

sentences.zh: 既而兵部疏請直省武職應依文官例，按年限由總督、提督會同舉劾。

translations.literal: Soon the Board of War memorialized that provincial military posts should follow civil precedent, with governors-general and provincial military commanders jointly recommending and impeaching according to years of service.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the Board of War proposed that provincial military officers follow civil precedent, with governors-general and provincial commanders jointly recommending and impeaching by years of service.

sentences.zh: 御史季振宜疏言：「武職考滿，營謀優等，剋扣軍饟，貽誤封疆。

translations.literal: Censor Ji Zhenyi memorialized: "In military completion of review, scheming for top grades, embezzling military pay, and harming frontier defense.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Ji Zhenyi memorialized: "In military completion reviews, officers scheme for top grades, embezzle army pay, and harm frontier defense.

sentences.zh: 請按歷俸功次升轉。

translations.literal: Request promotion and transfer according to salary history and merit ranking."
translations.idiomatic: Promotions should follow salary history and merit ranking."

sentences.zh: 」於是六年定舉行軍政事宜，京、外武職長官，註以四格，並詳列履行、軍功，分別去留，咨部。

translations.literal: Accordingly in the sixth year matters for conducting military inspection were fixed; capital and provincial military chiefs were noted according to four criteria, with service records and military merit listed in detail, retention or removal distinguished, and the matter communicated to the ministry.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 6 (1667) military inspection procedures were codified: capital and provincial military chiefs were rated by four criteria, with detailed service records and military merit, then retained or removed and reported to the Board.

sentences.zh: 必註明行止端方、弓馬嫻熟、管轄嚴肅、供職勤慎、不擾害地方等考語，方許薦舉。

translations.literal: Evaluation phrases such as upright conduct, skilled archery and horsemanship, strict jurisdiction, diligent service, and not harming the locality had to be noted before recommendation was permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Nominations required noting upright conduct, skilled archery and horsemanship, strict command, diligent service, and no harm to local populations.

sentences.zh: 必有八法等款實跡，始行糾參。

translations.literal: There had to be factual records under the eight categories before impeachment could proceed.
translations.idiomatic: Impeachment required factual records under the eight disciplinary categories.

sentences.zh: 復令提督、總兵官自陳，提督由總督註考，總兵官由總督、提督註考。

translations.literal: Provincial military commanders and regional commanders were again ordered to submit self-assessments; provincial commanders were evaluated by governors-general, regional commanders by governors-general and provincial commanders.
translations.idiomatic: Provincial and regional commanders submitted self-assessments; provincial commanders were evaluated by governors-general, regional commanders by governors-general and provincial commanders.

sentences.zh: 無總督省分，巡撫註考。

translations.literal: In provinces without a governor-general, the governor noted evaluations.
translations.idiomatic: In provinces without a governor-general, the governor recorded evaluations.

sentences.zh: 嗣以滇省用兵，海內騷動，羽書倥傯，軍政曠不舉行者十年。

translations.literal: Later, because Yunnan was at war and the realm was disturbed, urgent dispatches piled up, and military inspection was not conducted for ten years.
translations.idiomatic: War in Yunnan then disturbed the empire; urgent dispatches piled up, and military inspection was suspended for ten years.

sentences.zh: 至二十一年，滇逆蕩平，從給事中碩穆科請，舉行軍政大典，各官事實履行，自康熙十一年軍政後開起。

translations.literal: By the twenty-first year the Yunnan rebels were pacified; following Supervising Secretary Shuomuke's request, the great military inspection was held, with each officer's factual service record starting from after the Kangxi eleventh-year inspection.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 21 (1682), after the Yunnan rebellion was suppressed, Supervising Secretary Shuomuke's request restored the great military inspection, with service records dating from the Kangxi 11 inspection.

sentences.zh: 九門千總等由九門提督註考。

translations.literal: Battalion commanders of the Nine Gates and others were evaluated by the Nine Gates commander.
translations.idiomatic: Nine Gates battalion commanders were evaluated by the Nine Gates commander.

sentences.zh: 候補總兵官亦令自陳。

translations.literal: Candidate regional commanders were also ordered to submit self-assessments.
translations.idiomatic: Candidate regional commanders also submitted self-assessments.

sentences.zh: 副將以下候缺者，照舊例考察。

translations.literal: Brigade generals and below awaiting posts were examined according to old precedent.
translations.idiomatic: Brigade generals and below awaiting posts were examined under the old rules.

sentences.zh: 六十一年，命在京武職領侍衛內大臣，八旗都統，前鋒、護軍、步軍統領，副都統等，毋庸自陳。

translations.literal: In the sixty-first year, capital military officials including inner palace guards bearing the title of minister, Banner lieutenant-generals, vanguard, guard, and foot-soldier commanders, and deputy lieutenant-generals were ordered not to submit self-assessments.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 61 (1722), capital military officials including inner palace guard ministers, Banner lieutenant-generals, vanguard, guard, and foot-soldier commanders, and deputy lieutenant-generals were exempted from self-assessment.

sentences.zh: 考選軍政時，屬員註考，照外省舉劾例。

translations.literal: At military inspection selection, subordinates' evaluations followed the provincial recommendation and impeachment precedent.
translations.idiomatic: During military inspection, subordinates were evaluated under the same commendation and impeachment rules as provincial officials.

sentences.zh: 各省駐防將軍、副都統等，照提、鎮例自陳。

translations.literal: Garrison generals and deputy lieutenant-generals in the provinces submitted self-assessments following provincial and regional commander precedent.
translations.idiomatic: Provincial garrison generals and deputy lieutenant-generals submitted self-assessments like provincial and regional commanders.

sentences.zh: 屬員照京城例。
